{"preconditions": "1. Dark room environment
2. TV picture mode set to "HDR10 Pro"
3. A qualified HDMI HDR pattern generator supports HDR10 output; a separate calibrated photometer measures luminance", "steps": "【Separated Signal-Source and Measurement Setup】
1. Use an HDMI 2.1 cable to connect the qualified HDMI HDR pattern-generator output to the designated HDMI port on the LG OLED65C2LB TV
2. Place the calibrated photometer probe at the center of the TV screen
3. Power on the pattern generator and measurement instrument, wait for the instrument to complete startup (approx. 30 seconds)
4. Open the applicable generator or measurement control software, confirm the generator is connected and the separate photometer is online
5. In the software, select the "Brightness Measurement" module, set sampling interval 100ms
6. In the signal output module, select HDR10 format, load test video with complex light/dark scenes
7. Click "Send", prepare for comparative testing

【Formal Testing】
1. Send standard HDR10 test video (with complex light/dark scenes) from the qualified HDMI HDR pattern generator
2. First turn off HDR10 Pro, record the screen brightness distribution and tone curve
3. Turn on HDR10 Pro, send the same test video again
4. Use the separate calibrated measurement chain to compare the peak brightness, contrast, and tone mapping curve differences between the two modes", "expected": "1. After enabling HDR10 Pro, screen peak brightness increases
2. Dynamic contrast enhanced, highlights brighter, shadows deeper
3. Tone mapping curve optimized, highlight roll-off smoother
4. Color saturation and vibrancy moderately enhanced"}
items.reason: The Golden states a dark room, HDR10 Pro picture mode and a qualified HDR10 source chain.
